news.title: Acoramidis Shows Real-World Benefit Versus Tafamidis in ATTR-CM
news.summary: A peer-reviewed U.S. claims-data study comparing acoramidis (170 patients) with tafamidis (448 patients) in ATTR-CM found a 34% lower risk of a composite clinical-worsening endpoint (diuretic intensification, HF hospitalization, or death) with acoramidis, and a 43% lower risk of diuretic intensification alone. BridgeBio, which markets acoramidis, sponsored the analysis and cautioned that administrative claims data capture cardiac biomarkers poorly and that the 4.6-month average follow-up is short given acoramidis' recent approval.

news.title: Corcym reports first-in-human implant of Memo 4D Curve, an open-configuration mitral annuloplasty ring
news.summary: Corcym announced the first human implant of Memo 4D Curve, an FDA-cleared open-configuration addition to its Nitinol Memo mitral annuloplasty family, sized up to 42 mm for annuli ranging from standard degenerative disease to severely dilated. Michael Ibrahim performed the procedure at UVA Health; Corcym said it will formally introduce the ring internationally at the EACTS meeting in October 2026. No comparative outcomes data versus the existing closed Memo 4D ring were disclosed.

news.title: UBC's Heart Valve Performance Laboratory reports on a soft-closure mechanical valve prototype
news.summary: The University of British Columbia's Heart Valve Performance Laboratory described the design rationale and pulse-duplicator hydrodynamic testing of iValve, a bileaflet mechanical heart-valve platform built around curved leaflets and distributed, progressive closure contact intended to reduce the rapid-closure flow events linked to mechanical-valve thromboembolism and hemolysis. Prototypes maintained large projected opening areas across 10 test cycles at physiologic flow and pressure conditions. # needs-fulltext: abstract/metadata only, full text is paywalled.

news.title: Single-center study links TAVR performed more than 6 months after AS diagnosis to worse outcomes
news.summary: A retrospective single-center study of 149 severe aortic stenosis patients (2021-2023) found the composite of heart-failure hospitalization or death occurred more often when TAVR was performed more than 6 months after diagnosis (n=49) than within 6 months (n=100), over a median 729-day follow-up. Guidelines already call for surveillance within roughly 6-12 months for patients who do not meet immediate-intervention criteria; the authors say the findings support timelier evaluation but call for larger, multicenter confirmation given the small, single-site, non-randomized design.

news.title: Politecnico di Milano validates a balloon post-dilation model for patient-specific TAVI simulation
news.summary: Politecnico di Milano engineers, working with Ospedale Maggiore Policlinico, added a calibrated finite-element balloon model to patient-specific TAVI simulations to reproduce the post-dilation step that earlier simulation pipelines skipped. Predicted post-dilation valve configurations were compared against post-operative CT in four patients, and including the post-dilation step improved agreement between simulated and actual final device geometry. # needs-fulltext: abstract/metadata only, full text is paywalled.

news.title: ROS-responsive nanogel coating targets inflammation-driven bioprosthetic valve failure
news.summary: Sichuan University (West China Hospital) researchers compared explanted failed and non-degenerated bioprosthetic heart valves and found pronounced inflammation and reactive-oxygen-species accumulation in the failed leaflets. Guided by that finding, they built a ROS-responsive, diclofenac-releasing zwitterionic nanogel coating for glutaraldehyde-fixed pericardium designed to blunt inflammation-driven degeneration rather than only address calcification directly. # needs-fulltext: abstract/metadata only, full text is paywalled.

news.title: PEDIAVALVE project reports decellularized pulmonary valves sized for small children
news.summary: A Romania-based team (George Emil Palade University of Medicine, Targu Mures) working with Clemson University's Dan Simionescu published decellularization results for lamb pulmonary valves aimed at right ventricular outflow tract reconstruction in children, a size range under 15mm poorly served by current options. The protocol removed over 90% of donor DNA while preserving the valve's 3D matrix architecture, and decellularized valves matched fresh valves on opening area, pressure gradient, and 14-day cell viability in bench testing.

news.title: Large U.S. study highlights persistent heart-failure risk and underuse of guideline-directed therapy after TAVR
news.summary: An analysis of more than 37,000 U.S. TAVR patients found that heart failure remains common before and after valve replacement and that evidence-based HF medications are frequently underused. Within one year of TAVR, 18.6% experienced an acute HF episode; HF hospitalization and all-cause mortality reached 8.8% and 9.8% at one year, rising to 13.8% and 17.9% at two years.

news.title: Tempus receives ARPA-H award to test an autonomous AI agent in heart failure
news.summary: Tempus said an award of up to $9.5 million will support development and prospective multicenter validation of an AI agent intended to coordinate heart-failure care; the system remains investigational.

news.title: Corcym reports first-in-human implant of TriMemo, a dedicated tricuspid annuloplasty ring
news.summary: Corcym announced the first human implantation of TriMemo, a semi-rigid Nitinol annuloplasty ring purpose-built for tricuspid valve repair rather than adapted from a mitral design, performed by A. Marc Gillinov at Cleveland Clinic. The device received FDA clearance in April 2026 and is now commercially available in the US, extending Corcym's two-decade-old Memo mitral platform to the tricuspid valve; the release does not describe a pivotal trial or patient-selection criteria beyond this first case.

news.title: India launches national Valve Registry for transcatheter valve interventions
news.summary: India launched the India Valve Registry, a collaborative multicenter initiative designed to collect de-identified real-world data on patients undergoing transcatheter valve interventions and their long-term outcomes. The registry aims to generate India-specific evidence rather than relying primarily on European and North American datasets, and participating centers will contribute standardized treatment and outcome information.

news.title: LuX-Valve Plus TTVR expands into Eastern India with two high-risk cases
news.summary: Apollo Multispeciality Hospitals in Kolkata reported two consecutive transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement procedures using the Jenscare LuX-Valve Plus system in elderly, frail patients with severe symptomatic TR. Post-procedure assessments reportedly showed satisfactory valve function and resolution of significant regurgitation without major complications.

news.title: Medtronic invests up to $80M in Pi-Cardia and secures option to acquire the company
news.summary: Medtronic announced a strategic investment of up to $80 million in Pi-Cardia, developer of the FDA-cleared ShortCut leaflet-modification system used to enable valve-in-valve TAVR in patients at risk of coronary obstruction. Medtronic is expected to become the exclusive global commercial distributor for ShortCut in 2027, and the agreement includes an option to acquire Pi-Cardia for an estimated upfront price of up to $210 million, plus potential earn-outs.

news.title: Providence St. Joseph begins commercial use of Edwards SAPIEN M3 TMVR in Orange County
news.summary: Providence St. Joseph Hospital reported the first commercial SAPIEN M3 TMVR procedure in Orange County, California, expanding local access to Edwards Lifesciences’ FDA-approved transseptal mitral-replacement system. SAPIEN M3 is indicated for selected patients with symptomatic moderate-to-severe or severe MR who are unsuitable for surgery or TEER, and also for certain patients with mitral annular calcification.

news.title: LUMINARA Phase 2b Trial: Oral Relaxin Agonist AZD5462 Shows Early Promise in Heart Failure
news.summary: In the 375-patient LUMINARA Phase 2b trial, presented as an ESC 2026 Hot Line and published simultaneously in Circulation, AstraZeneca's oral RXFP1 relaxin-receptor agonist AZD5462 modestly improved a cardiac-remodeling measure (end-systolic volume index) in an HFrEF cohort (LVEF <=35%) and lowered systemic vascular resistance in a separate cohort with LVEF 41-55%, without excess hypotension or fluid retention. This was a dose-ranging safety/hemodynamic study, not powered for clinical outcomes, and the investigators said larger outcomes trials are now needed.

news.title: TRIC-I-HF shows transcatheter tricuspid repair can improve hard clinical outcomes
news.summary: TRIC-I-HF randomized 360 patients with symptomatic severe tricuspid regurgitation and elevated heart-failure risk to transcatheter tricuspid valve repair plus medical therapy or medical therapy alone. At one year, repair was superior on a hierarchical endpoint incorporating death, HF hospitalization and quality-of-life improvement, with a win ratio of 2.42. Longer-term follow-up also showed a lower risk of the composite of death or HF hospitalization through three years.

news.title: HELIOS-B Subgroup Shows Vutrisiran Benefit Holds Regardless of Background Tafamidis
news.summary: A prespecified HELIOS-B subgroup analysis presented at ESC Congress 2026 examined 654 ATTR-CM patients, 40% of whom were on background tafamidis, and found vutrisiran's effect on the composite of all-cause mortality and recurrent cardiovascular events through 33-36 months was consistent whether or not patients also took tafamidis. Alnylam, which markets vutrisiran, noted the trial was not statistically powered specifically for the tafamidis-combination subgroup and that health-status gains were attenuated in that group.

news.title: AI-supported monitoring of patients awaiting TAVI is linked to lower mortality
news.summary: ESC Congress featured new data showing that AI-supported monitoring of patients awaiting TAVI reduced mortality compared with conventional waiting-list management. The presentation sits within a broader ESC session focused on structural-heart imaging, artificial intelligence and procedural optimization, reflecting growing interest in digital tools that extend beyond CT sizing and into longitudinal patient management.

news.title: Bristol Myers Squibb Presents 5-Year Camzyos (Mavacamten) Data From EXPLORER-LTE at ESC 2026
news.summary: In the EXPLORER-LTE cohort of the MAVA-LTE extension study (231 patients followed up to 252 weeks), continuous mavacamten treatment was associated with sustained LVOT-gradient reduction, and 69.6% of patients improved by at least one NYHA class, with no new safety signals versus the original EXPLORER-HCM trial. Seven patients had reversible LVEF drops below 50% that recovered after treatment interruption, and Bristol Myers Squibb noted continued approval still depends on confirmatory post-marketing evidence.

news.title: ESC analyses extend aficamten evidence across obstructive and non-obstructive HCM
news.summary: Cytokinetics reported that ACACIA-HCM analyses showed changes in cardiac structure and diastolic function, while a MAPLE-HCM subgroup analysis favored aficamten over metoprolol across prior-treatment groups.

news.title: 2026 ESC Guidelines Redefine Heart Failure Classification, Drop HFmrEF Category
news.summary: The 2026 ESC Guidelines for the management of heart failure, published in the European Heart Journal and presented at ESC Congress 2026, collapse the three-way ejection-fraction classification into two phenotypes -- HFrEF (LVEF <50%) and HFpEF (LVEF >=50%) -- eliminating the separate HFmrEF category, and give mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (e.g., finerenone) a Class I recommendation across the EF spectrum. The guidelines also give semaglutide or tirzepatide a Class IIa recommendation in HFpEF patients with obesity, reflecting trial evidence rather than a formal drug-label change for that indication.

news.title: HighLife receives CE Mark for Clarity next-generation TMVR valve
news.summary: HighLife received CE Mark approval for its Clarity Mitral Heart Valve for use with the HighLife TMVR System. Clarity uses an open-cell outflow design intended to reduce left-ventricular-outflow-tract-obstruction risk while preserving HighLife’s transfemoral valve-in-ring architecture; the approved system covers native mitral annuli from 30 to 53 mm.

news.title: Abbott’s Amulet 360 LAA occluder receives CE Mark
news.summary: Abbott received CE Mark approval for Amulet 360, its next-generation dual-seal left atrial appendage occluder for patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation. The redesigned lobe is softer and more conformable, with smaller anchors intended to accommodate a broader range of LAA anatomies while retaining the outer disk as a second sealing layer.

news.title: New JACC analysis tests how robust the randomized evidence for mitral TEER really is
news.summary: Investigators reassessed COAPT, MITRA-FR, and RESHAPE-HF2 using fragility-index methods to quantify how resistant their conclusions are to small changes in event counts. COAPT’s reductions in heart-failure hospitalization and mortality remained comparatively robust, whereas several nonsignificant MITRA-FR outcomes were statistically fragile.

news.title: National real-world study sharpens the lifetime-management debate after TAVR
news.summary: A retrospective Epic Cosmos analysis included 300,927 TAVR patients treated from 2010 through May 2026 and examined long-term reintervention and clinically significant valve failure. Reintervention remained uncommon—1.2% at 5 years and 2.7% at 10 years—but 3,315 patients underwent redo-TAVR and 347 underwent surgical explantation.

news.title: PREVUE-VALVE shows AI-ECG structural-heart screening loses accuracy when moved into the community
news.summary: The PREVUE-VALVE study tested the EchoNext AI-ECG structural-heart disease model in a community cohort of adults aged 65–85 who received in-home ECG and echocardiography. Among 2,402 analyzable participants, structural-heart disease prevalence was only about 7.5% and the AI model’s discrimination fell to an AUC of 0.71, compared with approximately 0.83 in hospital-based cohorts; performance improved to about 0.79 in people with an abnormal ECG.

news.title: LuX-Valve Plus shows strong early outcomes in patients with very large tricuspid anatomy
news.summary: The European TRINITY cohort reported outcomes in 114 high-risk patients with severe or greater symptomatic tricuspid regurgitation treated using 55–70 mm LuX-Valve Plus systems, specifically addressing patients whose annuli are too large for many competing TTVR platforms. Intraprocedural success was 95.6%, 30-day clinical success was 91.2%, and 93.7% of patients had residual TR of moderate or less at 30 days.

news.title: Automated CT pipeline maps fibrocalcific burden ahead of TAVI
news.summary: Researchers at Vita-Salute San Raffaele University (Milan) built a one-click, CT-based pipeline that automatically segments and quantifies fibrotic and calcific tissue on the aortic valve from pre-TAVI cardiac CT, replacing a manual, radiologist-dependent step. In 25 patients with severe aortic stenosis the automated regional measurements agreed closely with two independent expert readers while processing each case in under three minutes. # needs-fulltext: abstract/metadata only, full text is paywalled.

news.title: Versa Vascular adds $15M to Series C and appoints former Medtronic structural-heart leader as CEO
news.summary: Versa Vascular appointed Bill Shields as CEO and announced a $15 million expansion of its Series C financing, bringing total committed capital in the round to $42 million. Shields previously spent 15 years at Medtronic and most recently led its Transcatheter Mitral and Tricuspid Therapies division. The new funding is earmarked for completion of the ongoing first-in-human study of the AdapTR transcatheter tricuspid repair system, a U.S.

news.title: Jupiter Endovascular recruits structural-heart trial leader to advance its Transforming Fixation catheter platform
news.summary: Jupiter Endovascular appointed interventional cardiologist Catalin Toma as chief medical officer. The company’s Transforming Fixation (TFX) platform is designed to let a catheter transition from flexible to fixed and back again, addressing the trade-off between navigation and procedural stability.

news.title: Review maps engineering path for soft robotic cardiac sleeves in heart failure
news.summary: A UNSW Sydney-led team, with Hannover Medical School, published a Nature Communications review of soft robotic cardiac sleeves, a non-blood-contact class of mechanical circulatory support that wraps and actuates around the outside of the heart. The review lays out the pathophysiological rationale, recent actuator and materials advances, and the engineering and translational hurdles still standing between prototypes and clinical use, and proposes a development framework for future devices.

news.title: Heart 'assembloids' give researchers a lab model of human valve disease
news.summary: University of Pittsburgh and Carnegie Mellon University researchers combined heart-chamber organoids grown from human stem cells into valve-bearing 'assembloids,' adding simulated blood flow and muscle contraction to reproduce native valve development. Introducing disease-linked mutations reproduced signs of mitral valve prolapse, offering a human tissue model for studying valve disorders without relying solely on animal studies. The work was published in Cell Stem Cell on August 11, 2026.

news.title: EARLY TAVR analysis shows treadmill testing can unmask treatment indications in “asymptomatic” severe AS
news.summary: A prespecified EARLY TAVR registry analysis found that treadmill stress testing identified an established indication for aortic valve replacement in roughly one in six patients initially considered asymptomatic with severe aortic stenosis. Of 1,250 screened patients, 146 had a positive stress test; among registry participants, 75.8% underwent AVR by six months, 79.9% by one year, and 85.9% by two years.

news.title: JACC publishes two-part best-practice framework for redo-TAVR
news.summary: A Heart and Valve Collaboratory consensus effort published a two-part technical framework for redo-TAVR, separating short-frame and tall-frame device combinations and emphasizing that TAV-in-TAV cannot be treated as a generic procedure. The documents standardize CT-based sizing and risk assessment, including implant-depth effects, neoskirt geometry, leaflet overhang, coronary access, sinus sequestration risk, anchoring, and second-valve expansion.

news.title: KU Leuven-led model simulates pulmonary-autograft dilation after the Ross procedure
news.summary: Engineers at KU Leuven, with Eindhoven University of Technology and Ghent University, built an image-based finite-element pipeline that reconstructs patient-specific root geometry and simulates how the pulmonary autograft grows and remodels under systemic pressure after a Ross procedure. The model reproduced observed autograft dilation in a sheep model and linked the predicted diameter change to leaflet coaptation loss, a step toward predicting which autografts will fail and require reoperation.

news.title: Asia-Pacific multicenter registry supports BASILICA and UNICORN leaflet modification for high-risk TAVR
news.summary: A multicenter Asia-Pacific registry reported real-world outcomes for transcatheter electrosurgical leaflet-modification techniques used to mitigate coronary obstruction during TAVR, including BASILICA and the newer UNICORN approach. The registry included 100 patients treated across seven centers; BASILICA was used in 67%, UNICORN in 30%, and a combined approach in 3%, with procedural success reported in 85.1% and 96.7% of BASILICA and UNICORN cases, respectively.

news.title: UC Davis performs first U.S. CARLEN procedure in Nyra Medical’s ENHANCE mitral-repair study
news.summary: UC Davis Medical Center reported the first U.S. treatment of symptomatic functional mitral regurgitation with Nyra Medical’s investigational CARLEN System as part of the ENHANCE Early Feasibility Study. CARLEN is a transcatheter, single-leaflet implant intended to restore mitral leaflet coaptation without sutures, tethers, or permanent alteration of the native valve anatomy, potentially preserving future treatment options. news.title: UC Irvine study evaluates polycarbonate-polyurethane scaffolds for polymeric mitral valves
news.summary: A UC Irvine biomedical engineering team led by Arash Kheradvar compared two polycarbonate-based polyurethanes as trileaflet scaffold materials for polymeric mitral valves, linking rheological and mechanical properties to valve-level flow, pressure, and wear performance out to 50 million accelerated cycles. One formulation was implanted in an ovine model as an early in-vivo check, part of a broader push toward polymeric valves that combine mechanical-valve durability with bioprosthetic-like hemodynamics.

news.title: Modular robotic steerable catheter platform demonstrates potential for complex endovascular access
news.summary: Researchers described a handheld robotic catheter with two steerable segments and four degrees of freedom, coupled to a modular tendon-driven actuation platform. The prototype was evaluated through simulation and in-vitro vascular-phantom testing for fenestrated and branched endovascular aneurysm repair.

news.title: ACC launches enhanced IMPACT Registry with a dedicated transcatheter pulmonary valve replacement option
news.summary: The American College of Cardiology released an enhanced version of the IMPACT Registry with more flexible data-collection pathways for interventional catheterization, electrophysiology, cardiac implantable electronic devices, and transcatheter pulmonary valve replacement. Programs can now select a submission pathway focused specifically on TPVR, which should reduce data-entry burden while preserving procedure-specific quality tracking.

news.title: Rare dual caval valve implantation performed for severe tricuspid regurgitation
news.summary: A multidisciplinary team at the Army Institute of Cardio-Thoracic Sciences in Pune reported a complex minimally invasive procedure in a patient with prior valve surgery and severe tricuspid regurgitation. The team implanted prosthetic valves in both the superior and inferior vena cava, creating a bicaval valve implantation strategy intended to reduce venous backflow without repeat open-heart surgery.

news.title: Edwards reports strong Q2 structural-heart growth and raises TAVR/TMTT guidance
news.summary: Edwards reported Q2 TAVR sales of $1.26 billion, up 11.3% year over year, and transcatheter mitral/tricuspid therapy sales of roughly $196 million, up about 47%. The company raised full-year TAVR growth guidance to 8%–9% and TMTT sales guidance to $760–$780 million. Edwards also highlighted upcoming TCT presentations for PROGRESS and CLASP IITR, expected U.S. approval of PASCAL for tricuspid use in Q4, and expected U.S./European approval of the next-generation PASCAL with Capture Clarity.

news.title: Boston Scientific starts FARADIGM IDE trial for Faraflex PFA system
news.summary: Boston Scientific enrolled the first patients in its FARADIGM IDE trial of the investigational Faraflex pulsed-field ablation catheter, with initial procedures performed at St. David’s Medical Center. Faraflex combines mapping and ablation in a single 8 Fr NAV-enabled catheter used with the Opal HDx mapping system. This is primarily an electrophysiology development rather than a structural-heart therapy milestone, so it is lower priority here.

news.title: Professional societies push CMS to preserve heart-team and registry safeguards in TAVR NCD update
news.summary: SCAI, ACC, and STS submitted joint comments supporting modernization of the U.S. TAVR National Coverage Determination while asking CMS to clarify several proposed changes. The groups recommended maintaining multidisciplinary heart-team evaluation, national-registry participation, and targeted coverage-with-evidence-development for selected populations. CMS is expected to issue a final decision around September 15, 2026.

news.title: ACC, SCAI, and STS submit formal comments on CMS’ proposed TAVR National Coverage Determination update
news.summary: The ACC, SCAI, and STS submitted joint comments to CMS on the proposed revision of the National Coverage Determination for TAVR. The societies support modernization of the policy but argue for preserving multidisciplinary heart-team decision-making, audited national registry participation, consistent quality standards, and continued clinical data collection.

news.title: Cytokinetics announces ESC 2026 late-breaking aficamten abstracts
news.summary: Cytokinetics announced planned ESC Congress presentations covering ACACIA-HCM and a MAPLE-HCM subgroup analysis, keeping cardiac myosin inhibition in focus ahead of the meeting.

news.title: Acoramidis analysis reports early, sustained kidney markers in ATTR-CM
news.summary: A BridgeBio-reported analysis describes an early reversible eGFR change and lower urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio through follow-up in ATTR-CM; it is supportive evidence, not a change to the approved indication.

news.title: STUN-AF suggests LAA ablation before LAAO may reduce peridevice leaks
news.summary: In the nonrandomized STUN-AF study, patients undergoing concomitant pulsed-field ablation and left atrial appendage occlusion had fewer peridevice leaks when the appendage was ablated before occlusion. The proportion with no leak was higher with LAA ablation at both 4 months and 12 months, and multivariable analysis associated LAA ablation with lower odds of leak.

news.title: First U.S. real-world TriClip data show strong commercial rollout
news.summary: TCTMD reported STS/ACC TVT Registry data for more than 3,000 patients treated with Abbott’s TriClip G4 system at 278 U.S. sites after FDA approval. Device success was 98%, 30-day all-cause mortality was 1.4%, median hospital stay was 1 day, and 96% of patients were discharged home. At 30 days, 87% had moderate-or-less TR and 51% had mild-or-less TR, with substantial improvements in KCCQ score and NYHA class.

news.title: Cardiawave begins routine European use of Valvosoft, a noninvasive ultrasound therapy for severe symptomatic AS
news.summary: Cardiawave announced routine clinical use of Valvosoft in France, the Netherlands, and Germany following CE marking in late 2025. The company says the system uses high-intensity ultrasound pulses to fragment calcification on native aortic-valve leaflets without surgery, implantation, or general anesthesia.

news.title: MassDevice frames the CMS proposal as a volume tailwind for major TAVR players
news.summary: MassDevice reported that analysts saw the CMS proposal as a positive for Edwards and the broader TAVR category, including Medtronic and Abbott; it also noted Boston Scientific’s potential re-entry via its MiRus investment. The article emphasized the removal of CED for symptomatic patients and the addition of a CED pathway for asymptomatic severe AS.

news.title: PREVUE-VALVE publication reinforces the scale of underrecognized valve disease
news.summary: PREVUE-VALVE used CVS and Walgreens outreach followed by at-home ECG and echocardiography in a national sample of adults aged 65–85. The study estimated moderate-or-greater valvular heart disease in 8.2% of this population and mild-to-moderate disease in 18.4%; tricuspid regurgitation was the most common moderate-or-greater lesion, followed by aortic stenosis and mitral regurgitation.

news.title: Ten-year PARTNER 2A and Sapien 3 registry data sharpen the TAVI durability discussion
news.summary: Ten-year follow-up showed that intermediate-risk patients treated with the older Sapien XT valve in PARTNER 2A had higher mortality and valve reintervention than surgical AVR overall, driven largely by transthoracic-access cases. In contrast, a propensity-matched comparison of the newer Sapien 3 registry cohort versus surgical AVR showed no difference in 10-year all-cause mortality or aortic-valve reintervention.

news.title: Anteris positions DurAVR around lifetime management and disease modification
news.summary: Anteris argued that as TAVR expands to younger, lower-risk patients, success metrics should extend beyond a technically successful implant to include hemodynamics, residual disease physiology, ventricular recovery, durability, and future intervention options. Its DurAVR is a balloon-expandable, single-piece biomimetic THV designed to mimic native-valve flow and is being studied in the PARADIGM trial against commercially available TAVR systems.

news.title: TRISCEND II analysis quantifies hospital-cost and length-of-stay drivers after Evoque TTVR
news.summary: A TRISCEND II analysis of 155 patients undergoing Edwards Evoque transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement found index-admission costs of about $80,005, including a $49,000 device-acquisition cost. New renal-replacement therapy and new pacemaker/CIED implantation were the largest independent contributors to incremental cost, while renal replacement, stroke, and new pacemaker/CIED implantation had the largest effects on length of stay.

entity.name: Atrial Fibrillation
entity.description: Most common sustained arrhythmia; thrombus typically forms in the left atrial appendage, the target of LAA closure for stroke prevention when anticoagulation is unsuitable.

entity.name: Patent Foramen Ovale (PFO-associated stroke)
entity.description: Residual interatrial communication implicated in paradoxical embolism and cryptogenic stroke; transcatheter closure reduces recurrent stroke in selected patients.

entity.name: Atrial Septal Defect
entity.description: Congenital opening in the atrial septum causing left-to-right shunt; secundum defects are amenable to transcatheter closure.

entity.name: Ventricular Septal Defect
entity.description: Congenital communication in the ventricular septum or, rarely, acquired septal rupture after myocardial infarction. Management depends on anatomy and hemodynamics; transcatheter closure is used for selected congenital defects and is an evolving option in some post-infarction cases.

entity.name: Patent Ductus Arteriosus
entity.description: Persistent fetal vessel connecting the aorta and pulmonary artery. Management depends on hemodynamic significance and patient age; in preterm infants, the benefits and timing of closure remain debated, with transcatheter closure considered for selected persistent hemodynamically significant cases.

entity.name: Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
entity.description: Sarcomeric cardiomyopathy with LV hypertrophy; the obstructive form (HOCM) features dynamic LVOT obstruction treated by septal reduction or cardiac myosin inhibitors.

entity.name: Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy
entity.description: Infiltrative cardiomyopathy from misfolded transthyretin (wild-type or hereditary) depositing in the myocardium; treated with TTR stabilizers and silencers.

data.label: Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction

entity.name: Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction
entity.description: Heart failure with left ventricular ejection fraction of 40% or less, managed with guideline-directed medical and device therapies tailored to the clinical profile.

data.label: Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction

entity.name: Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction
entity.description: Heart failure with left ventricular ejection fraction of 50% or greater and evidence of elevated filling pressures. Current treatment is guided by clinical phenotype and contemporary heart-failure recommendations.

entity.name: Coronary Microvascular Dysfunction & Refractory Angina
entity.description: Angina from impaired microvascular function (often with non-obstructive coronaries); device approaches include coronary sinus narrowing to redistribute perfusion.

entity.name: Aortic Stenosis
entity.description: Progressive narrowing of the aortic valve (commonly calcific/degenerative); severe symptomatic disease is treated by TAVR or surgical AVR, with trials now extending TAVR to low-risk and asymptomatic patients.

curation.notes: CMS finalized the NCD on 2026-09-10: Medicare covers TAVR for symptomatic severe AS without the former CED requirement, while asymptomatic severe AS remains covered only under CED in a CMS-approved study and with a device FDA-approved for that indication. This does not create unrestricted asymptomatic coverage. The 2026-06 proposed-NCD articles retained from the prior note are historical only.

entity.name: Aortic Regurgitation
entity.description: Diastolic backflow through an incompetent aortic valve causing LV volume overload; historically surgical, now with the first dedicated transcatheter device (JenaValve Trilogy) for symptomatic severe AR.

entity.name: Mitral Regurgitation
entity.description: Systolic backflow through the mitral valve, either primary/degenerative (leaflet/chordal) or secondary/functional (annular dilation, LV remodeling); treated by transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER), transcatheter replacement (TMVR), annuloplasty, or surgery.

entity.name: Mitral Stenosis
entity.description: Obstruction to LA-to-LV inflow, most often rheumatic (commissural fusion) or degenerative with mitral annular calcification; treated by percutaneous balloon commissurotomy or surgery.

entity.name: Tricuspid Regurgitation
entity.description: Backflow through the tricuspid valve, frequently functional from annular dilation/right-heart remodeling; long undertreated, now addressed by transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TriClip) and transcatheter replacement (EVOQUE).

entity.name: Pulmonary Valve Disease
entity.description: Pulmonary regurgitation/stenosis or RVOT conduit dysfunction, often in repaired congenital heart disease (e.g. tetralogy of Fallot); treated by transcatheter pulmonary valve replacement (Melody, Harmony) or surgery.

entity.name: Prosthetic paravalvular leak
entity.description: Regurgitant flow through a defect between a prosthetic valve and the native annulus, potentially causing heart failure or hemolysis; selected high-risk patients may undergo transcatheter closure.

entity.name: Ischemic left ventricular remodeling
entity.description: LV dilation and geometric distortion after extensive myocardial infarction; selected patients have been studied for surgical or hybrid scar exclusion and ventricular reconstruction.

entity.name: Systemic hypertension
entity.description: Persistently elevated systemic blood pressure is a cardiovascular risk condition that can cause target-organ injury, including left ventricular remodeling. Diagnosis requires confirmation using repeated or out-of-office blood-pressure measurements; the 2024 ESC guideline defines hypertension as office systolic pressure at least 140 mmHg or diastolic pressure at least 90 mmHg.

entity.name: WATCHMAN (original generation)
entity.regulatoryDetail: Original WATCHMAN received US FDA PMA P130013 in March 2015; distinct from the withdrawn 2015 FLX and FDA-approved 2020 FLX.

entity.name: ACASA-TAVI
entity.primaryEndpoint: Co-primary endpoints at 12 months: CT-detected hypoattenuated leaflet thickening (HALT; superiority) and a composite of VARC-3 bleeding, thromboembolic events, and all-cause death (noninferiority).
entity.outcomeSummary: In patients aged 65-80 without an independent anticoagulation indication after TAVI, 12 months of factor Xa DOAC monotherapy reduced HALT versus aspirin (16.2% vs 28.6%; risk ratio 0.55, 95% CI 0.37-0.82; P=0.004) and met noninferiority for the safety composite (7.5% vs 10.6%). These findings do not establish improved long-term valve durability or superiority for clinical events.

curation.notes: Procedure-level post-TAVI management evidence: the proc-tavi edge identifies the care setting, not a randomized comparison of TAVI devices or TAVI versus surgery. The registry permits clinician-selected therapeutic-dose apixaban, rivaroxaban, or edoxaban monotherapy versus aspirin 75 mg/day; it does not establish separate efficacy for each drug. The ClinicalTrials.gov record last updated June 9, 2026 reports completed status, actual enrollment of 360, and actual start December 4, 2021. It also lists 5- and 10-year MACE follow-up; those results are not reported here. JAMA reports 336 participants completing the trial. The safety risk difference was -3.3 percentage points (95% CI -9.5 to 2.8; noninferiority P<0.001). Low safety-event counts limit inference, and individual clinical components were not adequately powered. HALT is an imaging endpoint; do not generalize the result to all ages, anticoagulation regimens, or routine treatment recommendations.
